name: Netted Value-Momentum Combination
note: Two rank signals at deliberately opposite horizons on one symbol -- a long-horizon VALUE measure (today's price against a price average lifted from deep in the past) and a 2-to-12-month style MOMENTUM measure that skips the freshest window -- each converted to a percentile rank and NETTED into a single weight before any order exists. Cheap-and-rising gets roughly double weight; cheap-but-still-falling cancels to inside the no-trade band and is never traded. AMP rank the cross-section of an ETF universe; this feed is single-symbol, so the rank is against the measure's own trailing history instead, which keeps the netting structure and the opposite horizons and drops only the cross-sectional part. Horizons are in BARS, scaled so value stays several times longer than momentum.
source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen, 'Value and Momentum Everywhere' (Journal of Finance 2013), equation (3): r_COMBO = 0.5*r_VALUE + 0.5*r_MOM; equation (1) for rank weights; p. 938 for the 5-year value proxy and the choice of MOM2-12 as the momentum measure (the paper explicitly defends 2-12 over 7-12, citing Novy-Marx 2012 and Goyal & Wahal 2012).
code:
import math
import bisect


def _pct_rank(vals, w, minw):
    """Trailing percentile rank of each value against its own last w values."""
    n = len(vals)
    out = [None] * n
    win = []
    idxs = []
    for j in range(n):
        x = vals[j]
        if x is None:
            continue
        bisect.insort(win, x)
        idxs.append(j)
        if len(win) > w:
            old = vals[idxs[0]]
            del idxs[0]
            k = bisect.bisect_left(win, old)
            del win[k]
        m = len(win)
        if m >= minw:
            a = bisect.bisect_left(win, x)
            b = bisect.bisect_right(win, x)
            out[j] = (a + b) / (2.0 * m) - 0.5
    return out


def family_init(ctx):
    b = ctx.bars
    n = len(b)
    c = [float(x["c"]) for x in b]
    lc = [math.log(x) if x > 0 else 0.0 for x in c]
    mlb = int(ctx.p.mom_lb)
    msk = int(ctx.p.mom_skip)
    vlb = int(ctx.p.val_lb)
    vw = int(ctx.p.val_w)
    rn = int(ctx.p.rank_n)
    cs = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    for j in range(n):
        cs[j + 1] = cs[j] + c[j]
    V = [None] * n
    M = [None] * n
    for j in range(n):
        if j - mlb >= 0 and j - msk >= 0:
            # MOM(skip..lb): the long-horizon return that skips the freshest part
            M[j] = lc[j - msk] - lc[j - mlb]
        a0 = j - vlb - vw
        a1 = j - vlb
        if a0 >= 0 and c[j] > 0:
            # VALUE: how far today's price sits below a price average from
            # deep in the past -- the paper's 5-year-lagged price proxy
            mean = (cs[a1] - cs[a0]) / float(vw)
            if mean > 0:
                V[j] = math.log(mean / c[j])
    minw = max(30, rn // 4)
    rv = _pct_rank(V, rn, minw)
    rm = _pct_rank(M, rn, minw)
    bl = float(ctx.p.blend)
    wv = [None] * n
    for j in range(n):
        if rv[j] is None or rm[j] is None:
            continue
        # rank weights, centred, then NETTED at the position level before any
        # order exists: cheap-and-falling cancels to nothing and is not traded
        wv[j] = 2.0 * (bl * rv[j] + (1.0 - bl) * rm[j])
    ctx.w = ctx.series(wv, "netted_weight")
    ctx.rv = ctx.series(rv, "value_rank")
    ctx.rm = ctx.series(rm, "mom_rank")


def signal(ctx, i):
    w = ctx.w[i]
    if w is None:
        return 0
    band = float(ctx.p.band)
    if w > band:
        return 1
    if w < -band:
        return -1
    return 0
